new.n: Indian pony trail crossing, Raccoon Creek, 1845 GLO survey
new.pl: Line between secs. 29 and 30, 74.30 ch north of the 29/30/31/32 corner, T14N R6W, Vernon County (1845 GLO field notes)
new.v: Trade beads, gun flints, lost horse gear
new.st: The 1845 government survey notes for T14N R6W record a measured Native trail. On the line north between secs. 29 and 30, at 74.30 chains, the surveyor crossed an "Indian pony trail, deep, bears West". The same "pony trail" crosses the line between secs. 20 and 29 three more times, at 40.10, 50.00 and 63.00 chains (bearing S70W, N80W and SW), and the quarter post there was set "in mound". A trail worn "deep" was in long use. The same notes show that the mark on the plat at the sec. 29/30 line near Raccoon Creek is a pond 200 links across that drains into the creek, not a mill or dam.
new.t: Follow the trail line across sec. 29 on the LiDAR for a worn trace. Look only from the road, or ask the landowner first. Private land.
src: GLO interior field notes T14N R6W, Wisconsin (1845), lines secs. 29/30 and 20/29, UW Digital Collections
pinev: Field-note crossing on the sec. 29/30 line at 74.30 ch, placed from the BLM PLSS corner (about 50 m); the trail runs on west and crosses the 20/29 line three times.
